title: The AI Agent Every Company is About to Build | Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch

bestTimestamp.label: Introduction to Company Agents
bestTimestamp.rationale: The video starts immediately with the concept of agents running a company and sets the stage for the discussion.

insights.title: AI Agents as Killer Apps
insights.description: AI agents are emerging as 'killer apps' for building software and running companies, similar to word processors for PCs or new use cases for mobile.

insights.title: Internal Company Brain Agent
insights.description: Vercel uses an internal 'V' agent that acts as a knowledge base, data analysis, and project management tool, helping employees navigate company information and tasks.

insights.title: The Evolution of 'V' to 'Eve'
insights.description: Vercel developed its internal 'V' agent and then created 'Eve,' a framework to democratize agent building, making it easier for anyone to create and deploy their own agents.

insights.title: God Agent vs. Team of Agents
insights.description: The ideal agent experience is a 'god agent' (like Star Trek's computer) that acts as a router, delegating tasks to various specialized sub-agents while managing access control and identity.

insights.title: Agents as Proactive Tools
insights.description: Future agents will be proactive, performing tasks like social media monitoring or report generation in the background, rather than just responding to prompts.

insights.title: Importance of Secure Connectivity
insights.description: The biggest challenge in building agents is securely connecting them to internal systems, defining governance, data access, and security models.

insights.title: Cost and Speed of AI Models
insights.description: The declining cost and increasing speed of AI models, particularly open-source ones, are significant advancements that will make agents more effective and accessible.

chapters.name: Introduction: The Rise of AI Agents
chapters.description: Guillermo Rauch, CEO of Vercel, discusses the growing importance of AI agents in business and introduces Vercel's internal agent, highlighting its capabilities and impact.

chapters.name: AI Agents as Killer Applications
chapters.description: Rauch explains how AI agents are becoming killer applications, drawing parallels to past technological shifts like personal computers and mobile phones, with a focus on coding agents and 'run your company better' agents.

chapters.name: Vercel's Internal 'V' Agent
chapters.description: The discussion delves into Vercel's internal 'V' agent, an omni-present intelligence in Slack that helps employees with tasks, acting as a router to various specialized sub-agents.

chapters.name: Challenges in Implementing AI Agents
chapters.description: The host asks about the difficulties of implementing AI agents for teams, particularly regarding permissions and integrating personal skills, prompting Rauch to explain Vercel's approach.

chapters.name: The 'Soul' of an Agent: Eve Framework
chapters.description: Rauch introduces 'Eve,' Vercel's framework for building agents, emphasizing the concept of 'soul.md' files that define an agent's genesis and the importance of giving agents a secure, serverless computing environment.

chapters.name: God Agent vs. Team of Agents
chapters.description: The conversation addresses whether to build one 'god agent' or a team of agents, with Rauch advocating for a central routing agent that manages access and delegates to specialized tools based on context.

chapters.name: Building and Maintaining Your Own Agent
chapters.description: Rauch explains how to start building an Eve agent by defining its instructions, adding tools (like WordPress integration), and setting up communication channels, while also managing guardrails and human approvals.

chapters.name: Proactive Agents and Self-Improvement
chapters.description: The discussion shifts to the concept of proactive agents that perform tasks autonomously and the importance of self-improvement for agents, including methods for evaluation and feedback.

chapters.name: Accessibility of Agent Building
chapters.description: Rauch believes agent building will become democratized, with everyone able to create basic agents, while technical experts focus on core system loops, data access, and security.

chapters.name: Getting Started with Eve
chapters.description: Rauch encourages listeners to try Eve.dev, connect an agent to a chat medium, and automate a 'toil task' as a starting point, sharing an example of Vercel's agent assisting with product changelogs.

chapters.name: Future of AI: Cost and Speed
chapters.description: The conversation concludes with Rauch's excitement about the decreasing cost and increasing speed of AI models, likening the current state to the early days of the iPhone.

chapters.name: Model Agnosticism and Optimization
chapters.description: Rauch highlights the benefit of model agnosticism in Eve, allowing users to choose the best models for different tasks (fast for interactive, accurate for asynchronous) and benefit from market competition.
